messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — autoscaler ceiling hit for gpu-pool-west-1. policy=max-nodes, current=48, limit=48, pending queue growth detected. priority=high. paging on-call.

Ryan (oncall): seeing a bunch of 429s and enqueue growth in the ingest queue. queue length ~5.2k, avg wait ~18s. Routing to infra.

Ben (infra): I can see the autoscaler logs showing repeated 'scale suppressed: reached max nodes'. Cloud quota is fine, this is our configured ceiling. What's the customer impact?

Maya (support): Affected customers flagged: Finly-payments (production), EduApp-batch (staging->prod syncs delayed). Finly's throughput errors are triggering error-rate alerts. Finly reports increased end-user latency.

Carla (eng-sre): copy. Pulling per-pool metrics. Visual: CPU/GPU util ~85-95% across pool, pods Pending=120. Pod events: FailedScheduling -> Insufficient nodes.

Trish (product): is there any auto-fallback to smaller models? Should we route some requests to lower-cost model variants to reduce queue?

Ben (infra): we have a rollout policy but automatic fallback is off for this tier — past incidents caused quality regressions. Can do manual fallback if needed. Proposing temporary cap raise to 70 nodes while we drain queue.

Ryan (oncall): +1 to raise. Need to coordinate with infra lead for manual override. Also will notify Finly via status page update that we're mitigating.

Carla (eng-sre): I'll request a manual patch to the autoscaler cap. Patch will update cluster-autoscaler configmap: `spec.maxNodes: 48 -> 70`. Applying now with rollback plan.

Ben (infra): FYI command I'll run to validate after patch:
```
kubectl -n kube-system get configmap cluster-autoscaler -o yaml | yq .data
# then kubectl apply -f autoscaler-cap-bump.yaml
```

Maya (support): posting an interim status to status.redwood.com: "Investigating increased inference latency in GPU cluster west-1; mitigation in progress."

Carla (eng-sre): Applied patch, config map updated. cluster-autoscaler logs showing scale decision -> adding nodes. New target maxNodes=70.

incident-bot: Update — nodes provisioning started. estimated time to ready ~7-12m per node depending on image.

Ryan (oncall): Watching the pending queue. Any sign of pods scheduling?

Ben (infra): Node join events coming in. 6 nodes ready in the last 4 minutes. Pod pending count dropped from 120 -> 68.

Trish (product): Noted. Let us know if we need to trigger model fallback. Prefer to avoid if we can.

Maya (support): Finly acknowledged status update and is monitoring. No immediate escalations from them yet.

Carla (eng-sre): Node join steady. Pods scheduling. Queue length dropped to ~900, avg wait 4s. Will keep cap at 70 for 30 minutes then evaluate rollback to 50.

Ben (infra): Added temporary Cloud runlimit increase ticket to keep an eye on costs (internal). Also leaving autoscaler logging in debug for next 30m.

Ryan (oncall): handing off to overnight SRE: @Carla you're owning post-provision monitoring and rollback. If queue flares back, escalate to oncall lead.

Carla (eng-sre): taking handoff. I'll post a follow-up summary and the commands used.

incident-bot: Incident thread marked 'mitigating'. Incident ID: INC-2026-1948501234.

Carla (eng-sre): summary for the runbook: manual cap raise from 48->70 applied to cluster-autoscaler configmap at 1948501378. Nodes provisioned; queue drained. Next steps: 1) monitor for 30m 2) evaluate permanent policy change if frequent 3) schedule postmortem with product & support.

Maya (support): I'll prepare customer impact notes for postmortem (timeouts, affected customer list, timestamps).

Trish (product): Please include traffic spike context — looks like a batch job from EduApp overlapped with a Finly promotion. Need to consider rate-limiting knobs per-tenant.

Ben (infra): leaving debug logs and the autoscaler snapshot in S3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/INC-2026-1948501234/.

Carla (eng-sre): resolved-for-now. Keeping incident open for monitoring window. If everything is green at 30m, I'll rollback cap to 50 and close.

incident-bot: Note — don't forget to run the post-incident checklist: oncall handoff, customer comms, root-cause analysis, and timeline.
